chunks: From him, from his father, from Suleyman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida, from his father (peace be upon them), who said:

A group of people were presented to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) during one of his military expeditions, so he said: 'Who are these people?' They said: 'Believers, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'And what has reached of your faith?' They said: 'Patience during affliction, and gratitude during prosperity, and contentment with the divine decree.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Forbearing, knowledgeable. They are so close to the Prophets through their jurisprudence that if you are as you describe yourselves, do not build what you will not dwell in, and do not amass what you will not consume, and fear Allah, to whom you will be returned.'
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of true faith and the Prophet's advice on wealth in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the profound spiritual maturity of believers, characterizing them as 'wise scholars' whose depth of understanding (fiqh) approaches that of the Prophets. The Prophet’s advice to avoid building what one does not inhabit and accumulating what one does not consume reflects the Shia emphasis on detachment from worldly excess (zuhd) while maintaining active faith. This narrative reinforces the concept that true piety is measured by contentment with divine decree (rida) rather than material accumulation.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, from his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> father<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘A group of people came up to Rasool-Allahsaww during one of hissaww military expeditions, so hesaww said: ‘Who are these people?’ So they said, ‘Momins, O Rasool-Allahsaww! Hesaww said: ‘And what has reached from your Emān?’ They said, ‘The patience during the afflictions, and the gratefulness during the prosperity, and the pleasure with the Ordainment’.

So Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘Forbearing, knowledgeable. The understanding is almost as if it could happen to be of Prophets<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, if you are just as you are describing (yourselves to be). So, do not build what you would not be living in, and do not amass what you would not be consuming, and fear Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, the One to Whom you will be returning’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from him from his father from Sulayman al-Ja’fary from abu al- Hassan al-Rida from his father (a.s.) who has said the following:

“A people came to the Messenger of Allah during one of the armed expeditions and he asked who are these people? They said, ‘Believers, O Messenger of Allah.’ He then asked, ‘What is the degree of your belief?’ They replied, ‘It is patience in hardships, thankfulness in prosperous life and agreement with the decision of Allah.’

The Messenger of Allah then said, ‘These are forbearing and knowledgeable people. Their understanding is almost to the degree of the prophets. If you really are what you say you are, do not build what you will not use for dwelling, do not accumulate what you will not eat and be pious before Allah to whom you will return.’”
